article_content: Despite a rise in credit card fraud, the most commonly used PIN remains '1234', with '1111' and '0000' following closely. DataGenetics' research on 3.4 million four-digit PINs revealed that one in ten codes can be guessed on the first attempt. The study found that over a quarter of PINs can be guessed within 20 attempts, partly because many users choose birth years as their PINs.

article_content: Clermont Foot have named former France captain Corinne Diacre as their new coach, replacing Helena Costa who stepped down this week. Costa became the first female coach of a professional men's club in the top two tiers of any European league when she was appointed by Clermont last month, but the 36-year-old quit on Monday citing personal reasons. French second division club Clermont have now given the job to another female, with 39-year-old Diacre taking up the role. Diacre made 121 appearances for France between 1993 and 2005, while as a coach she has been an assistant to the national team for the last seven years as well as managing her former club Soyaux since 2010. A statement on www.clermontfoot.com read: 'Corinne Diacre has accepted the position of coach of Clermont Foot 63 for the next two seasons and will take up the post early next week.'

article_content: Researchers have made a significant discovery off Queensland's coast, revealing that hidden groundwater discharge is a major contributor to the nutrient overload in the Great Barrier Reef. The study, led by Dr. Douglas Tait from Southern Cross University, found that this underwater discharge is 10 to 15 times higher than the nutrients coming from rivers. The team used radium isotopes to track the nutrient flow from underground aquifers and sediments, showing that groundwater accounts for about one-third of the Reef's nitrogen and two-thirds of its phosphorous. This challenges current conservation efforts, which have primarily focused on river outflows. Experts warn that excess nutrients can lead to issues like 'harmful algal blooms, crown-of-thorns starfish outbreaks, and fish diseases,' highlighting the need for a new management strategy.

article_content: At 70 years old, Bob Yelton is demonstrating remarkable courage by participating in this week's World Amateur Handicap Championships. Just before the tournament, Yelton's wife of 22 years, Martha, fell ill and passed away. Despite having 'no interest in playing golf' due to his loss, encouragement from his brother Don and son Porter prompted him to attend. Porter told him 'Mum would have wanted you to play,' motivating him to participate. In April, Yelton suffered a heart attack while playing golf, but thanks to prompt medical attention, he recovered. The World Amateur Handicap Championships brings together nearly 3,100 golfers from 25 countries and 49 U.S. states to Myrtle Beach.

article_content: (CNN) -- A 478-carat diamond was unearthed in Lesotho, potentially yielding one of the largest and highest quality round polished diamonds, according to Gem Diamonds Ltd. The diamond was analyzed in Antwerp, Belgium, and determined to be of the highest color grading. 'What makes it remarkable is the color and quality,' said Neil Buxton. 'It's a D color, the highest grading, and we believe there's a good chance of getting a 100-carat plus round stone.' The diamond ranks as the 20th largest rough diamond ever found and was discovered in September at the Letseng Mine.

'رنگ و کیفیت آن قابل توجه است'، گفت نیل باکستون. 'رنگ D دارد که بالاترین درجه است و معتقدیم احتمال دستیابی به یک الماس 100 قیراطی تراش خورده وجود دارد.' این الماس بیستمین الماس خام بزرگ کشف شده است.

article_content: It was a mother's worst nightmare. On March 31, 2014, at 11 p.m., I received a distressing phone call from my 25-year-old son, Andrew. 'Mom, I've gotten lost and made a wrong turn, ending up at the Mexico border. I've been surrounded by military personnel, and I need you to know what's happening in case anything happens to me.' The next day, I received another call. 'Mom, I've been arrested. Please get me an attorney,' Andrew said. This was the most frightening call of my life, even more so than the call from Afghanistan when he told me, 'We've just been hit by an IED.' Three days later, a call from La Mesa Prison in Tijuana, Mexico, left me shaken: 'Mom, I'm not going to make it through the night. Whatever you do, don't come down here and ask questions or investigate, as you'll be killed too.' As Independence Day passes this year, it's bittersweet to think about my son being detained due to a felony arrest in a foreign country while we navigate a foreign judicial system. It's inconceivable to think about my vibrant and ambitious son being held in incarceration. This young man, who valiantly fought for others' freedom in two tours in Afghanistan and was meritoriously promoted to sergeant on the battlefield in 2012, is now languishing in a Mexican prison. He's been there since April 1, 2014, for inadvertently crossing the border with legally purchased firearms. This separation is far more traumatic than his combat tours. In Afghanistan, he had his Marine Corps brothers watching his back. Now, I feel like our executive branch has abandoned him, which feels inhumane. A petition on Whitehouse.gov garnered nearly 130,000 signatures, but the White House hasn't responded. Secretary of State John Kerry raised Andrew's issue with Mexican authorities during a trip to Mexico in May. I'm outraged. Andrew's situation should be considered grave, serious, and urgent. Over the years, reading scripture, I'd often pause at the directive to visit those in prison, wondering how, who, and why. Now, I've learned to walk without shame through the corridors of bars and locks, gaining a new perspective on incarceration. Incarcerating a loved one is a heart-wrenching experience that can debilitate and consume both the captive and their loved ones. It's a difficult journey, but there's rest in understanding that God's timing is perfect. This comfort keeps me going. The saying 'Trust his heart when you can't trace his hand' is something I've had to rely on. Through faith, I'll continue to persevere. My strength comes from the Lord and the solidarity of many on both sides of the border and around the world. I'm not alone; having shared my heartache with many, it feels like they've cupped my tears and replenished me with hope and support.

'مامان، گم شدم و یک پیچ اشتباه زدم و به مرز مکزیک رسیدم. افراد نظامی اطراف من هستند و می‌خواهم بدانی اگر اتفاقی برایم افتاد.' روز بعد، تماس دیگری گرفتم. 'مامان، من دستگیر شدم. لطفا یک وکیل بگیر.' این ترسناک‌ترین تماس زندگی من بود. سه روز بعد، تماسی از زندان لا میسا در تیخوانا، مکزیک، مرا تکان داد: 'مامان، من از این شب جان سالم به در نمی‌برم. هر کاری می‌کنی، نیا اینجا و سوال نکن یا تحقیق نکن.' در تعطیلات روز استقلال، فکر کردن به پسرم که به دلیل یک دستگیری جنایی در یک کشور خارجی زندانی است، بسیار تلخ است. تصور کردن پسر پرشور و بلندپروازم من در زندان غیرقابل تصور است. او از 1 آوریل 2014 به دلیل عبور غیرعمدی از مرز با سلاح‌های گرم قانونی زندانی شده است. این جدایی بسیار دردناک‌تر از دوره‌های جنگ اوست. اکنون، احساس می‌کنم شاخه اجرایی ما او را رها کرده است. یک طومار در Whitehouse.gov نزدیک به 130,000 امضا جمع‌آوری کرد، اما کاخ سفید پاسخی نداد. وزیر امور خارجه، جان کری، موضوع اندرو را در سفری به مکزیک در ماه مه با مقامات مکزیکی مطرح کرد. من عصبانی هستم. وضعیت اندرو باید جدی و فوری تلقی شود.

article_content: The U.S.-led coalition fighting ISIS in Syria has intensified its airstrikes on the militant group's de facto capital, Raqqa, with reports indicating 30 airstrikes overnight. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights, based in London, confirmed this escalation. Another opposition group in Raqqa mentioned that around 30 airstrikes by 'the international coalition' targeted areas northwest of the city. Previously, the coalition primarily targeted Kobani, near the Turkish border. The increase in activity in Raqqa comes after nearly 100 people were killed in Syrian government airstrikes last week, with many more critically injured. The Syrian government carried out at least 10 airstrikes, hitting key locations such as the al-Hani Mosque and the public market. Raqqa serves as a strategic location for ISIS, housing training centers, weapons depots, and fighter accommodations. The Syrian conflict has entered its third year, with government forces clashing with ISIS and other rebel groups. On Sunday, fighting continued across Syria, resulting in over 40 deaths from airstrikes, shelling, and raids. A leader of Jabhat al-Nusra, an al Qaeda affiliate, was among those killed north of Aleppo.

article_content: By Tara Brady. PUBLISHED: 13:32 EST, 14 February 2013. UPDATED: 13:39 EST, 14 February 2013. A bullet signed by former Navy SEAL sniper Chris Kyle was auctioned for '$24,000', eight days after his death. Chris Kyle, 37, who completed four tours in Iraq and wrote 'American Sniper', was killed by a fellow veteran at a North Texas gun range. Kyle was considered the deadliest sniper in U.S. military history. The bullet was bought by Lubbock lawyer Allen Adkins, who matched a bid of '$12,000'. Adkins stated, 'I cherish this in the sense that I'm honoured to be associated with a great American.' The proceeds will go to the Heartline Women's Clinic. Chris Kyle's funeral procession was attended by around 200 vehicles.

article_content: Jan Pfrimmer, 72, has lived in various places. She traveled the US as a 'flying trapeze' artist, lived in Mexico City, dealt cards in Reno and Tahoe, and worked as an accountant near San Diego. Pfrimmer, who spent most of her life in California, moved to Shepherdstown, West Virginia, a small town with 1,500 residents. She said California had become too expensive and stressful, with long commutes and wildfires. In contrast, West Virginia offered a lower cost of living, friendly people, and a slower pace of life. Pfrimmer sold her California home for $630,000 and bought a larger townhouse in West Virginia for $285,000. She appreciates the simple aspects of her new life, like the sound of trains and nature's beauty.

article_content: With Arsenal's passage to the Champions League knockout phase already assured, Arsene Wenger has named six rising stars from the club's academy for Tuesday's match against Galatasaray. Chuba Akpom, 19, is an English striker who has had significant exposure to Arsenal's first team. Gedion Zelalem, 17, is a German midfielder signed by Arsenal in 2013. Ainsley Maitland-Niles, 17, is an English winger who has been on the bench for Arsenal's senior team. Stefan O'Connor, 17, is an English defender established in Arsenal's Under-21 team. Alex Iwobi, 18, is a winger born in Nigeria but represents England. Glen Kamara, 19, is a Finnish defensive midfielder expected to make his first-team debut.

article_content: New research suggests that certain chemicals in sunscreen may impair male fertility. A study involving 501 couples found that men exposed to BP-2 or 4OH-BP experienced a 30% reduction in fertility. These chemicals are commonly used in sunscreens, shampoos, and moisturisers to protect against sun damage. Experts recommend continued sunscreen use for skin cancer prevention but suggest limiting exposure to UV filters for fertility concerns.

Tests found 'at least' 57 schools had 'alarmingly elevated' copper and lead levels; 17 others are still being tested. City officials blame 'outdated' fixtures, but many question this 'simplistic' explanation, pointing to Flint as an example of government 'incompetence.' Until completion, 'safe' bottled water will be provided to affected schools. The district will replace over 800 drinking fountains with hydration stations, a 'long-term solution' critics call a 'band-aid fix.' Hydration stations use 'advanced' filtration technology to remove contaminants. Superintendent Vitti said installation should be complete by end of next summer, but many are skeptical, much like they were in Flint. This isn't Michigan's first water contamination issue; Flint's 2014 water switch had 'devastating' consequences, and many say Detroit is 'following in its footsteps.' article_content: By RFE/RL's Radio Farda November 02, 2023 Iran is carrying out executions 'at a terrifying rate,' putting to death at least 500 people in the first seven months of the year, United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said in a new report, which shows a 50 percent increase in capital punishment over the same period in 2022. The rate of executions in Iran has been rising sharply, particularly in the wake of widespread protests after the death of 22-year-old Mahsa Amini in Tehran in 2022 while in the custody of the notorious Iranian morality police for an alleged hijab infraction. The authorities have responded to the unrest with a brutal crackdown that has left thousands dead and tens of thousands injured. Guterres said in a report to the UN General Assembly that seven men were executed in relation to or for participating in protests sparked by Amini's death. In all seven cases, information received 'consistently indicated that the judicial proceedings did not fulfill the requirements for due process and a fair trial under international human rights law,' he said. The data was first published in October in a report by Javaid Rehman, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran. It said that there was evidence of 'confessions extracted through torture and of the death penalty having been implemented after court proceedings that substantially violated the right to fair trial.' The UN secretary-general also cited information received by the UN rights agency that between September 17, 2022, and February 8, 2023, an estimated 30,000 individuals were arrested for participating in the protests. 'It is particularly concerning that most of the individuals arrested may have been children, given that the reported average age of those arrested was estimated to be 13 years, according to the deputy commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps,' Guterres said. Guterres cited reported instances of disproportionate and excessive use of force against protesters, and beatings and sexual violence after they were put in detention, as well as psychological abuse. 'Access to adequate and timely legal representation was frequently denied, with reports of coerced confessions, which may have been obtained as a result of torture,' he also said. Guterres expressed deep concern 'at the lack of transparent and independent investigations into reported human rights violations, in particular in the context of the latest nationwide protests.' He said the continued targeting of lawyers is also impeding accountability for past and ongoing violations. The secretary-general also said that 300 people -- more than half of those executed in the first seven months of 2023 -- were reportedly put to death for drug-related offenses. The October report by the UN special rapporteur on Iran said that the number of those executed from ethnic minority communities, in particular the Baluch minority, remained 'disproportionately high,' especially for drug-related or security-related offenses. Amnesty International has said the regime in Tehran executes more people than any other country in the world other than China, and decried a situation that has turned the country's prisons into 'killing fields.' The U.S.-based Center for Human Rights in Iran has said politically motivated executions in Iran are increasing 'dramatically' as authorities use capital punishment as a 'tactic of intimidation and retribution.' translated_content: 'ایران با سرعتی وحشتناک اعدام ها را انجام می دهد,' به گزارش دبیرکل سازمان ملل متحد آنتونیو گوترش در گزارش جدیدی که نشان می دهد 50 درصد افزایش در مجازات اعدام در مدت مشابه در سال 2022 وجود دارد. نرخ اعدام ها در ایران به شدت افزایش یافته است، به ویژه پس از تظاهرات گسترده پس از مرگ مهسا امینی 22 ساله در تهران در سال 2022 در حالی که در بازداشت پلیس اخلاق ایران بود. مقامات به شورش ها با سرکوب وحشیانه ای پاسخ داده اند که هزاران کشته و ده ها هزار زخمی برجای گذاشته است. گوترش در گزارشی به مجمع عمومی سازمان ملل گفت که هفت مرد در ارتباط با یا برای شرکت در تظاهرات ناشی از مرگ امینی اعدام شدند. در همه هفت مورد، اطلاعات دریافتی 'به طور مداوم نشان داد که دادرسی قضایی الزامات فرآیند دادرسی و محاکمه عادلانه تحت قوانین بین المللی حقوق بشر را برآورده نمی کند,' او گفت. این داده ها برای اولین بار در اکتبر در گزارشی توسط جاوید رحمان، گزارشگر ویژه سازمان ملل در مورد حقوق بشر در ایران منتشر شد. گزارش شده است که شواهدی از 'اعترافات گرفته شده از طریق شکنجه و اجرای مجازات اعدام پس از دادرسی دادگاه که به طور قابل توجهی حق محاکمه عادلانه را نقض کرده است,' وجود دارد. دبیرکل سازمان ملل همچنین به اطلاعات دریافت شده توسط آژانس حقوق بشر سازمان ملل اشاره کرد که بین 17 سپتامبر 2022 و 8 فوریه 2023، حدود 30,000 نفر به دلیل شرکت در تظاهرات دستگیر شدند. 'به ویژه نگران کننده است که اکثر افراد دستگیر شده ممکن است کودکان بوده باشند، با توجه به اینکه میانگین سن دستگیر شدگان 13 سال تخمین زده شده است، طبق گفته معاون فرمانده سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی,' گوترش گفت. گوترش به موارد گزارش شده از استفاده نامتناسب و بیش از حد از زور علیه معترضان، و ضرب و شتم و خشونت جنسی پس از بازداشت، و همچنین سوء استفاده روانی اشاره کرد. 'دسترسی به نمایندگی قانونی کافی و به موقع اغلب انکار شد، با گزارش هایی از اعترافات اجباری که ممکن است در نتیجه شکنجه به دست آمده باشند,' او همچنین گفت. گوترش نگرانی عمیق خود را 'از عدم تحقیقات شفاف و مستقل در مورد نقض حقوق بشر گزارش شده، به ویژه در زمینه آخرین تظاهرات سراسری,' ابراز کرد. او گفت که ادامه هدف قرار دادن وکلا نیز مانع پاسخگویی برای نقض های گذشته و جاری می شود. دبیرکل همچنین گفت که 300 نفر -- بیش از نیمی از کسانی که در هفت ماه اول سال 2023 اعدام شدند -- به دلیل جرائم مربوط به مواد مخدر اعدام شدند. گزارش اکتبر توسط گزارشگر ویژه سازمان ملل در مورد ایران گفت که تعداد اعدام شدگان از جوامع اقلیت های قومی، به ویژه اقلیت بلوچ، 'به طور نامتناسبی بالا' باقی مانده است، به ویژه برای جرائم مربوط به مواد مخدر یا امنیت. عفو بین الملل گفته است که رژیم در تهران بیش از هر کشور دیگری در جهان به جز چین اعدام می کند و وضعیت را محکوم کرده است که زندان های کشور را به 'میدان های کشتار' تبدیل کرده است. مرکز حقوق بشر در ایران که مستقر در ایالات متحده است، گفته است که اعدام های با انگیزه سیاسی در ایران به طور 'دراماتیک' افزایش می یابد زیرا مقامات از مجازات اعدام به عنوان 'تاکتیک ارعاب و انتقام' استفاده می کنند.

article_content: ASUNCION - Security forces have completely taken over Paraguay's Congress on Tuesday as lawmakers fiercely debated a possible change in law that would allow President Horacio Cartes to run for re-election, a move vehemently condemned by the opposition as a 'dictatorial grab for power'. A bill allowing presidents to run for a second five-year term was previously defeated, but Cartes' allies are desperate to revive it. This week, a group of senators requested a special session, seen by the opposition as a clear sign of Cartes' plan to undermine democracy. Paraguayans participating in the 'Long March' protest chanted 'Cartes out' and held signs saying 'Democracy in Danger'. Opposition leaders accused Cartes of staging a coup by surrounding Congress with police and soldiers. Cartes, a wealthy soft drink and tobacco mogul, was elected in 2013, and his backers won't stop until he gets re-elected. Critics argue that changing the constitution for Cartes' benefit is unfair and undemocratic. The Inter-American Development bank's regional meeting in Asuncion is expected to be overshadowed by the protests. Security firms warned conference attendees to steer clear of the Congress area due to imminent violence. Thousands of farmers are set to arrive in Asuncion to demand radical agrarian reform. Cartes' supporters vowed to fight on for the rule change, claiming it's a matter of democratic rights.

article_content: Thai Prime Minister Srettha Thavisin is set to introduce a bill next week to 'fully legalize' same-sex marriage, positioning Thailand as a potential 'trailblazer' in the region. Both Thavisin and his opponents have vowed to 'expand and safeguard' LGBTQ rights. Thavisin announced on X (formerly Twitter) that his cabinet will debate the marriage equality bill the following week. A spokesman for the prime minister told the Bangkok Post that if the cabinet approves, the bill will be presented to parliament in December. 'I believe this is a crucial step towards a more 'inclusive and equal' society,' Thavisin stated, revealing plans to follow the marriage bill with two additional legislative proposals: one to simplify the process for transgender individuals to update their gender on official documents, and another to 'regulate and legalize' prostitution. The marriage equality bill is expected to face minimal opposition in parliament, backed by Thavisin’s 11-party coalition and opposition leader Pita Limjaroenrat’s eight-party alliance. Thailand boasts a 'vibrant' gay subculture, highlighted by this year’s Bangkok Pride parade, which drew over 50,000 participants. However, the country's laws remain 'conservative and outdated,' failing to recognize civil unions or cohabitation between same-sex couples. Prostitution is currently 'illegal,' yet it is openly practiced in Thai bars and tourist areas. The government also does not acknowledge sex changes, despite an estimated 315,000 transgender individuals residing in Thailand. Thailand's neighbors do not recognize same-sex marriage, with severe penalties for homosexuality in Malaysia and Myanmar. Taiwan and Nepal are the only Asian countries granting same-sex couples equal legal rights to heterosexual couples. Thavisin also announced the formation of a 'high-level committee' to推进 gender equality and expressed interest in hosting the 2028 World Pride festival.

'من معتقدم این گامی مهم به سوی جامعه‌ای 'فراگیر و برابر' است،' تاویسین اظهار داشت و از برنامه‌ریزی برای دو پیشنهاد قانونی دیگر پس از لایحه ازدواج خبر داد: یکی برای تسهیل فرآیند تغییر جنسیت افراد ترنس‌جندر در اسناد رسمی، و دیگری برای 'تنظیم و قانونی کردن' روسپی‌گری. انتظار می‌رود لایحه برابری ازدواج با مخالفت حداقلی در پارلمان مواجه شود، زیرا ائتلاف 11 حزبی تاویسین و اتحاد هشت حزبی رهبر اپوزیسیون، پیتا لیمجارنرات، از آن حمایت می‌کنند. تایلند دارای یک فرهنگ غنی همجنس‌گرایان است که در جشنواره پراید بانکوک امسال با حضور بیش از 50,000 نفر برجسته شد. با این حال، قوانین این کشور هنوز 'محافظه‌کارانه و قدیمی' هستند و اتحادیه‌های مدنی یا هم‌زیستی بین زوج‌های همجنس را به رسمیت نمی‌شناسند. روسپی‌گری در حال حاضر 'غیرقانونی' است، اما به طور آشکار در بارها و مناطق توریستی انجام می‌شود. دولت همچنین تغییرات جنسی را به رسمیت نمی‌شناسد، علی‌رغم وجود حدود 315,000 فرد ترنس‌جندر در تایلند. همسایگان تایلند ازدواج همجنس‌گرایان را به رسمیت نمی‌شناسند و مجازات‌های سنگینی برای همجنس‌گرایی در مالزی و میانمار وجود دارد. تایوان و نپال تنها کشورهای آسیایی هستند که حقوق قانونی یکسانی را برای زوج‌های همجنس به مانند زوج‌های دگرجنس‌گرا قائل هستند. تاویسین همچنین از تشکیل یک 'کمیته ویژه' برای پیشبرد برابری جنسیتی خبر داد و ابراز علاقه کرد که میزبان جشنواره پراید جهانی 2028 باشد.

article_content: Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice is 'set to visit Europe' this week as a 'political storm' brews on the Continent over 'unsubstantiated claims' that the United States 'may be maintaining' secret prisons in Eastern Europe to hold suspected terrorists. VOA'S Peter Fedynsky 'examines the controversy' and its 'potential impact' on Secretary's European agenda. Secretary Rice 'reportedly discussed' allegations of secret U.S. prisons in Europe last week with visiting German Foreign Minister Frank-Walter Steinmeier. Germany is one of several European allies that have 'called for clarity' on reports of such facilities. The Bush administration 'has not confirmed nor denied' the allegations, but the United States 'has promised to respond' to European concerns. State Department spokesman Sean McCormack said, 'These are certainly legitimate questions that are posed by the press and publics and we will do our best to respond to those questions.' On November 2nd, the Washington Post 'cited unnamed U.S. and foreign officials' saying that the Central Intelligence Agency 'has been accused of hiding and interrogating some of its most important al Qaeda captives at a Soviet-era compound in Eastern Europe.' Human Rights Watch 'claims to have found some evidence' pointing 'potentially' to Poland and Romania as possible sites. Polish President Alexander Kwasniewski and Romanian Prime Minister Calin Tariceanu 'have denied any knowledge' of secret CIA prisons in their countries. But Human Rights Watch 'points to some flight logs' which indicate that the CIA flew a Boeing 737 aircraft on an 'indirect route' from Afghanistan to Guantanamo Bay, Cuba with 'some unexplained stops' in Szymany Airport in Northeastern Poland and the Mihail Kogalniceanu military airfield in Romania on September 22, 2003. The organization 'has compiled a list' of 26 detainees allegedly held incommunicado by the CIA, including Ramzi Binalshibh, a suspected co-conspirator in the September 11th attacks on the United States. James Carafano, an anti-terrorism expert at the Heritage Foundation, 'questions the validity' of flight logs and prisoner lists as proof of the existence of secret prisons. 'These allegations have been made before,' said Mr. Carafano. 'What you have is people coming forward who seem incredibly credible: representatives of the United Nations, representatives from non-governmental organizations, and they say 'we've heard enough of these stories, so we think it's credible.'' Tom Malinowski of Human Rights Watch 'stresses the importance' of an explanation for the United States. 'The United States derives its moral authority from the perception that it stands for basic principles of democratic governance, human rights, respect for the law.' Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice 'is scheduled to advance' U.S. interests beginning Monday with a five-day trip to Germany, Romania, Ukraine and Belgium. James Carafano 'believes that' the current uproar in Europe over secret prisons 'should not overshadow' the Secretary's trip. 'Fundamentally, the U.S. and Europe are moving in the same direction on terrorism.' But EU officials 'are taking the allegations seriously' enough to have threatened to cut off EU voting rights for any member country found to allow secret prisons on its soil.
translated_content: 'وزیر امور خارجه کندولیزا رایس قرار است این هفته به اروپا سفر کند' در حالی که 'طوفانی سیاسی' در قاره اروپا در مورد 'ادعاهای بی اساس' مبنی بر اینکه ایالات متحده 'ممکن است در حال نگهداری' زندان های مخفی در اروپای شرقی برای نگهداری تروریست های مشکوک است، شکل گرفته است. پتر فدینسکی از VOA 'به بررسی این جنجال' و 'تاثیر بالقوه آن' بر برنامه های وزیر در اروپا می پردازد. وزیر رایس 'گفته می شود که در مورد' ادعاهای مربوط به زندان های مخفی ایالات متحده در اروپا هفته گذشته با وزیر امور خارجه آلمان، فرانک والتر اشتاین مایر، گفتگو کرده است. آلمان یکی از چندین متحد اروپایی است که 'شفافیت بیشتری را درخواست کرده اند' در مورد گزارش های مربوط به چنین تاسیساتی. دولت بوش 'این ادعاها را نه تایید کرده است و نه رد کرده است'، اما ایالات متحده 'متعهد شده است که به نگرانی های اروپایی ها پاسخ دهد'. سخنگوی وزارت امور خارجه، شان مک کورمک، گفت: 'اینها قطعا سوالاتی قانونی هستند که توسط مطبوعات و عموم مردم مطرح می شوند و ما بهترین تلاش خود را برای پاسخ به این سوالات خواهیم کرد.' در 2 نوامبر، واشنگتن پست 'به نقل از مقامات آمریکایی و خارجی نامعلوم' گزارش داد که آژانس اطلاعات مرکزی 'متهم به پنهان کردن و بازجویی از برخی از مهم ترین اسیران القاعده در یک مجموعه مربوط به دوران شوروی در اروپای شرقی است.' دیده بان حقوق بشر 'ادعا می کند که برخی شواهد' را یافته است که 'به طور بالقوه' به لهستان و رومانی به عنوان مکان های احتمالی اشاره می کند. رئیس جمهور لهستان، الکساندر کفاشنیفسکی، و نخست وزیر رومانی، کالین تاریچانو، 'هرگونه اطلاع از زندان های مخفی سیا در کشورهای خود را انکار کرده اند'. اما دیده بان حقوق بشر 'به برخی از گزارش های پروازی' اشاره می کند که نشان می دهد سیا یک هواپیمای بوئینگ 737 را در یک 'مسیر غیرمستقیم' از افغانستان به گوانتانامو بی، کوبا با 'برخی توقف های غیرقابل توضیح' در فرودگاه شیمانی در شمال شرقی لهستان و پایگاه هوایی میخائیل کوگالنیچانو در رومانی در 22 سپتامبر 2003 پرواز داده است. این سازمان 'لیستی تهیه کرده است' از 26 بازداشت شده که ادعا می شود توسط سیا به طور غیرقانونی نگهداری می شوند، از جمله رمزی بنالشیب، مظنون به توطئه در حملات 11 سپتامبر به ایالات متحده. جیمز کارافانو، کارشناس ضد تروریسم در بنیاد هریتیج، 'اعتبار گزارش های پروازی و فهرست زندانیان را به عنوان اثبات وجود زندان های مخفی زیر سوال می برد'. 'این ادعاها قبلا نیز مطرح شده است،' آقای کارافانو گفت. 'شما افرادی را دارید که رو به جلو می آیند و به نظر می رسد بسیار معتبر هستند: نمایندگان سازمان ملل، نمایندگان سازمان های غیردولتی، و آنها می گویند 'ما به اندازه کافی از این داستان ها شنیده ایم، بنابراین فکر می کنیم قابل باور است'.'' تام مالینوفسکی از دیده بان حقوق بشر 'بر اهمیت' توضیح برای ایالات متحده تاکید می کند. 'ایالات متحده اقتدار اخلاقی خود را از این تصور که پایبند اصول پایه ای حکومت دموکراتیک، حقوق بشر، و وی احترام به قانون است، به دست می آورد.' وزیر امور خارجه کندولیزا رایس 'برنامه ریزی کرده است تا' منافع ایالات متحده را از روز دوشنبه با یک سفر پنج روزه به آلمان، رومانی، اوکراین و بلژیک پیش ببرد. جیمز کارافانو 'معتقد است که' هیاهوی کنونی در اروپا بر سر زندان های مخفی 'نباید بر سفر وزیر سایه افکند'. 'اساسا، ایالات متحده و اروپا در جهت همان مبارزه با تروریسم حرکت می کنند.' اما مقامات اتحادیه اروپا 'این ادعاها را به اندازه کافی جدی گرفته اند' تا تهدید کنند که حقوق رای دهی اتحادیه اروپا را برای هر کشور عضوی که اجازه دهد زندان های مخفی در خاک آن فعالیت کند، قطع کنند.

Massimo Viglione, CEO at Reios, praised the acquisition as a 'major stride forward', confirming Reios' dedication to an 'indispensable' IoT platform. Robert Schena, CEO and Co-founder of Rajant, called it a 'groundbreaking' opportunity to deepen their global presence.

article_content: People in the northeastern U.S. city of Boston will look forward to the arrival of spring Friday after enduring the city's 'most catastrophic' winter season snowfall on record. A 'monster storm' on Sunday dropped another 7.4 centimeters of snow, pushing the total since November to 275.8 centimeters. That is more than double Boston's average of 'a meager' 110 centimeters of snow in a season. Boston Mayor Marty Walsh joked about the new record on Twitter, comparing the wintry milestone to Boston's recent string of 'questionable' major sports championships. 'There will be no parade,' he wrote. The season actually started slow with Boston getting less than a centimeter of snow in December at its international airport where the official data is recorded. But in a three-week stretch starting January 25, the city endured a 'brutal and unprecedented' stretch of multiple storms that dropped a combined 217 centimeters of snow. That helped the month of February become Boston's snowiest since the previous record in 'the infamous winter of' 1995-96.

article_content: By Giulia Petroni Shares in 'Volkswagen Group' fell on Monday after the 'leading German carmaker' adjusted its full-year guidance for operating profit due to being severely hit by 'unprecedented flooding' in Slovenia and 'significantly higher' product costs. At 0849 GMT, the stock traded 2.85% lower at EUR100.20. Volkswagen said it expects to post an operating result of 4.9 billion euros ($5.19 billion) in the quarter, with an operating return on sales of around 6.2%, according to preliminary figures. For 2023, the group now expects the operating result to be around the previous year's level of EUR22.5 billion. The company had previously forecast an operating return on sales between 7.5% and 8.5%, equating to between EUR23.6 billion and EUR26.7 billion according to analysts. 'The warning is a clear sign of broader sector issues,' Deutsche Bank analysts said. article_content: HARARE - Zimbabwe's military 'promised' Wednesday to 'maintain transparency' in upcoming elections and denied it would 'influence nationwide voting' scheduled for July 30 as the opposition 'expressed concerns' about 'unfair polls'. The military is under 'close observation' following its 'brief intervention' in November that led to the 'ouster' of former president Robert Mugabe. Previous elections under Mugabe were 'marred by controversy', intimidation and 'alleged fraud' -- often attributed to the security forces. 'The Zimbabwe Defense Forces has no direct role in the upcoming elections,' said army spokesman Overson Mugwisi at a media conference in Harare ahead of the presidential, parliamentary and local polls. 'We are disturbed by 'unsubstantiated reports' alleging that the Zimbabwe Defense Forces is going to be used by (the ruling) ZANU-PF to 'manipulate the vote'. Following the military's statement, the leader of the main opposition Movement for Democratic Change (MDC) party Nelson Chamisa said it would 'reconsider its participation' in 'elections that lack credibility' and raised the prospect of calling for the election to be 'overseen by an external body'. 'We will not go into an election that has its own 'irregularities',' he said, casting doubt on the work of the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission but signaling his 'trust in the military'. 'We are going to be tempted to ask the South African Development Community (SADC) and African Union (AU) to 'supervise' the vote,' said Chamisa, referring to the regional and continental blocs. He also called for the ZEC, which he has previously accused of being 'biased', to store and distribute ballot papers more 'securely'. 'We therefore call upon SADC, the AU and the international community to 'intervene and ensure a credible process' and 'prevent a legitimacy crisis',' he said. The army appears to have staged its media briefing in response to a report in the Standard daily that it had 'allegedly deployed personnel' to rural areas to 'campaign for ZANU-PF candidates'. The Standard said it had received complaints from defeated contenders for the ZANU-PF slate. They reported that some winning candidates who were former senior military officers had been 'using the army to win the primary elections,' it said. 'If some serving members are participating in the ongoing political campaigns, they will be doing so 'illegally' and not as a result of an 'official instruction' from their commanders,' said Mugwisi. 'The conduct of the Zimbabwe Defense forces after elections is going to be guided by the 'principles of the constitution'. July's polls will be the first ballot box test for Mnangagwa, and the first since Mugabe was 'removed from office' after 37 years in power. President Emmerson Mnangagwa, 75, has 'assured' to hold 'transparent and fair' elections as he seeks to 'improve international relations'. But the main opposition remains 'unconvinced' by his stated commitment to 'democratic principles'. 'What we are currently witnessing is a regime that simply 'talks about reform' but does not intend to hold 'credible elections',' added Chamisa. But Chamisa signaled his 'confidence in the military', saying he was 'not worried'. 'They are a 'patriotic and professional' army. They are a 'respected institution', I work with the army very well. In fact, I 'have great respect for them',' he said.
translated_content: هاراره - ارتش زیمبابوه روز چهارشنبه 'تعهد کرد' که در انتخابات آتی 'شفافیت را حفظ کند' و انکار کرد که در رای‌گیری سراسری برنامه‌ریزی شده برای 30 ژوئیه 'تاثیر بگذارد'، همزمان اپوزیسیون 'نگرانی‌هایی' درباره 'انتخابات ناعادلانه' ابراز کرد. ارتش تحت 'نظارت دقیق' پس از 'مداخله کوتاه‌مدت' خود در نوامبر که منجر به 'برکناری' رئیس‌جمهور سابق رابرت موگابه شد، قرار دارد. 'نیروهای دفاعی زیمبابوه هیچ نقش مستقیمی در انتخابات آتی ندارند,' گفت سخنگوی ارتش، اورسون موگویس در یک کنفرانس مطبوعاتی در هاراره قبل از انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری، پارلمانی و محلی. 'ما از گزارش‌های 'تایید نشده' مبنی بر اینکه نیروهای دفاعی زیمبابوه توسط (حزب حاکم) ZANU-PF برای 'دستکاری رای' استفاده خواهند شد، ناراحت هستیم. پس از بیانیه ارتش، رهبر حزب اصلی اپوزیسیون، جنبش برای تغییر دموکراتیک (MDC)، نلسون چامیسا، گفت که در 'انتخابات‌هایی که فاقد اعتبار هستند' 'شرکت خود را مجددا بررسی خواهد کرد' و احتمال درخواست برای نظارت خارجی بر انتخابات را مطرح کرد. 'ما وارد انتخاباتی که 'بی‌نظمی‌هایی' دارد نخواهیم شد,' او گفت، و در عین حال به کار کمیسیون انتخابات زیمبابوه شک کرد اما اعتماد خود را به ارتش ابراز کرد. 'ما وسوسه خواهیم شد که از جامعه توسعه جنوب آفریقا (SADC) و اتحادیه آفریقا (AU) بخواهیم که رای را 'نظارت کنند,' گفت چامیسا، به بلاک‌های منطقه‌ای و قاره‌ای اشاره کرد. او همچنین از ZEC، که قبلا آن را 'سوگیری' متهم کرده بود، خواست تا برگه‌های رای را به طور 'امن‌تر' ذخیره و توزیع کند. 'بنابراین ما از SADC، AU و جامعه بین‌المللی می‌خواهیم که 'مداخله کنند و یک فرآیند معتبر را تضمین کنند' و 'از بحران مشروعیت جلوگیری کنند',' او گفت. به نظر می‌رسد ارتش کنفرانس مطبوعاتی خود را در واکنش به گزارشی در روزنامه استاندارد که گفته بود ارتش 'به طور ادعایی پرسنل را به مناطق روستایی برای 'کمپین برای کاندیداهای ZANU-PF' اعزام کرده است، برگزار کرده است. استاندارد گفت که شکایاتی از سوی کاندیداهای شکست خورده برای فهرست ZANU-PF دریافت کرده است. آنها گزارش دادند که برخی از کاندیداهای پیروز که افسران ارشد نظامی سابق بودند، 'از ارتش برای پیروزی در انتخابات اولیه استفاده کرده‌اند,' گفت. 'اگر برخی از اعضای خدمت‌رسان در کمپین‌های سیاسی جاری شرکت می‌کنند، آنها به طور 'غیرقانونی' و نه به عنوان نتیجه یک 'دستور رسمی' از سوی فرماندهان خود عمل خواهند کرد,' گفت موگویس. 'رفتار نیروهای دفاعی زیمبابوه پس از انتخابات توسط 'اصول قانون اساسی' هدایت خواهد شد'. رای‌گیری ژوئیه اولین آزمون جعبه رای برای مناناگاگوا خواهد بود و اولین بار پس از آن است که موگابه پس از 37 سال از قدرت 'برکنار شد'. رئیس‌جمهور امرسون مناناگاگوا، 75 ساله، 'اطمینان داده است' که انتخابات 'شفاف و عادلانه' برگزار کند، زیرا تلاش می‌کند روابط بین‌المللی را 'بهبود بخشد'. اما اپوزیسیون اصلی همچنان 'قانع نشده است' از تعهد او به 'اصول دموکراتیک'. 'چیزی که ما در حال حاضر شاهد آن هستیم یک رژیم است که صرفا 'در مورد اصلاح صحبت می‌کند' اما قصد ندارد 'انتخابات معتبر' برگزار کند,' افزود چامیسا. اما چامیسا اعتماد خود را به ارتش ابراز کرد و گفت که 'نگران نیست'. 'آنها یک ارتش 'وطن‌پرست و حرفه‌ای' هستند. آنها یک 'نهاد محترم' هستند، من با ارتش خیلی خوب کار می‌کنم. در واقع، من 'احترام زیادی برای آنها قائلم',' او گفت.

'ما نسبتاً مطمئن هستیم که مضر نیست، با احتمال 99 درصد.' سرویس تحقیقات فدرال این ماده را به عنوان مدرک تحلیل خواهد کرد. کنگره در تعطیلی به سر می‌برد و پلیس به طور موقت کاپیتول را به عنوان یک اقدام احتیاطی تعطیل کرد که هزاران کارمند را تحت تأثیر قرار داد. در اکتبر، کارکنان سنا به دلیل احتمال قرار گرفتن در معرض سیاه‌زخم، پس از دریافت نامه به دفتر داشل، درمان شدند. تاکنون هیچکس متهم نشده است و بسیاری از کارشناسان بر این باورند که این یک 'عملیات درونی' بوده و به منابع موثق استناد می‌کنند. تحقیقات همچنان بر روی سایر موارد مشکوک به سیاه‌زخم که منجر به مرگ پنج نفر شده، ادامه دارد. برخی گمانه‌زنی‌ها حاکی از یک 'عملیات پرچم دروغین' است که توسط یافته‌های اخیر پشتیبانی می‌شود.
